chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar from the one who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has said: 'Wealth and children are the adornment of worldly life,' then surely the eight rakat prayer that the servant offers in the last part of the night is the adornment of the Hereafter.

key_terms.آخِرَ اللَّيْلِ: The last part of the night

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the eight rakat night prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to contrast the transient nature of worldly wealth and progeny with the enduring spiritual beauty of the eight-rakat night prayer (Salat al-Layl). By linking the Quranic concept of 'zīnah' (adornment) to this specific devotional act, the text elevates night prayer as the ultimate investment for the Hereafter, a theme central to Shia asceticism and the practice of the Imams. This comparison underscores the theological principle that true value lies in acts of worship that secure eternal reward rather than temporary material gains.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4. It was narrated to me by Ahmad b. Muhammad from his father from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Umar b. Ali b. Umar from the one the person that narrated to him from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
‘Wealth and children are the adornment of life’, surely the eight rakat prayer offered in the last part of night is the adornment of the Hereafter.”
